as वासुदेव. Boyish sports in व्रज, charged with eating mud; lived with Nanda and his wife who were the same द्रोण and धरा born as Nanda and यशोदा by the command of ब्रह्मा. When once यशोदा left the churning pot to mind the boiling milk overflowing in the oven, कृष्ण broke the curd pot and ran away with butter to feed a monkey. So he was bound with a rope to an उलूखल (mortar) but the rope always fell two inches [page१-437+ ४०] short in spite of bits being added. At last कृष्ण pitied her and allowed himself to be tied; with the mortar he passed between two tall Arjuna trees, when down fell the trees, out of which emerged two men Nalakubera and मणिग्रीव (sons of Kubera) who had been cursed by नारद. कृष्ण blessed them and sent them back to their abode.
१०: भा. X.
Chaps. 8, 9
and १०; Vi.

-१९.
Enjoyed the company of Gopis singing and dancing. Gifts on his जन्मनक्षत्र day. Noticed a Daitya in the guise of a calf and taking him by the tail, he whirled him to death and flung the body on the top of a कपिथ tree. On another occasion Asura Baka met him in the guise of a crane, when कृष्ण tore its jaws asunder. Once when in the forest with his playmates, Agha, an asura friend of कंसा took the form of a boa-constrictor with a view to devour the cattle and all boys together. All of them entered his open mouth with कृष्ण who took his life out of his body and came out to the wonderment of gods. The अजागर skin when dried was a cave for Vraja people. Agha, however, attained salva- tion.
११: भा. X. Chap. II.
One day the boys sat and ate merrily when the cattle had gone far into the hill and dale and कृष्ण promised to bring them back. In the meantime ब्रह्मा had them hidden. So कृष्ण created duplicates of the cattle and the children that had been lost. These went home as usual and this continued for a year, when ब्रह्मा released the hidden cows which suckled their calves, and came to see the child, the one Brahman without a second, and belauded the baby Hari, and returned to his region. More boyhood sports.
१२: Ib. X. Chaps. १३ and १४; Vi.
. ३० to the end of
Chap. 9

.
In regularly tending cows, imitated voice of beasts and birds in ब्रिन्दावन just like a rustic. Once the cattle drank of the poisonous waters of the यमुना and became unconscious. After reviving them he found the reptile कालीय in the waters. He immediately jumped into the pool and was enclosed in its coils. At this Nanda and the whole Vraja moved to the banks of the river with great concern. [page१-438+ ३९] राम advised them to be cool. Slowly कृष्ण brought the reptile under his control, and getting on its hood, began to dance, when the कालीय acknowledged defeat. Finding his end near, कालीय's wives prayed to कृष्ण to spare him. The generous Lord allowed him to make his abode in the sea, thus purifying the यमुना once for all.
१३: भा. X. Chaps. १५ and १६. Vi.

(whole).
After this incident the whole Vraja was encamped for the night in that vicinity. A forest fire attacked the camp, when कृष्ण swallowed it and protected its inmates. His dances and songs; other past-times. Among the games was one in which the victor rode on the back of the vanquished. कृष्ण carried श्रीदाम on his back.
१४: भा. X. Chaps. १७ and १८.
Once again the cattle went astray in the thick forest, and surrounded by fire they bellowed in thirst and hunger. कृष्ण and his playmates found it impossible to reach the spot. So कृष्ण got upon a tree and called the cattle by names, and they responded. Asking his followers to shut their eyes, he swallowed the forest fire. When they opened their eyes, they found themselves in their homes.
१५: Ib. X. १९. 1-१३.
कृष्ण filled ब्रिन्दावन with गान्धर्वन् music and played at times on flute. Hid the clothes of Gopis who observed कात्यायनि व्रत to get him as their husband, and returned them only when they saluted with their two hands over their heads as a penance for bathing naked during the period of a व्रत। It was a severe day in summer when some Gopas approached him for food. कृष्ण advised them to go to the neighbouring यज्ञशाल and ask for food, sing- ing the praises of बलराम and himself. The sacrificers were silent at their request. कृष्ण asked them to repeat their request to ladies in his name. The ladies took four kinds of food and in spite of protest by their male relations, they came to have दर्सन् of the Lord and placed before Him all the eatables. On कृष्ण's advice they went back to com- plete the sacrifice, and assured them of their being accepted by their relations and the world. Their male relations [page१-439+ ३९] regretted having missed a chance of meeting the Lord. Then food was distributed among his friends.
१६: भा. X. Chaps. २१-23.
कृष्ण saw the Gopas worshipping Indra and as resi- dents of hills and forests, he suggested worship of mountains and cows. When this was accepted, Indra sent a heavy downpour which was warded off by कृष्ण, a boy of seven,
१७: Ib. X. Chaps. २४-26; Vi. V. १०. २५-41; ११. १६-25; १

.
holding up the Govardhana for a week. A visit from Indra and Surabhi who anointed him, Indra, of Goloka and gave him a new name Govinda. Rescued his father Nanda from वरुण region and took him with other Gopas to Brahma- ःरद where the Vedas were praising Hari. Once when playing on a flute, the गोपीस् who were in the midst of house- hold duties stopped them and came to where he was in spite of protest from their male relations. कृष्ण advised them to go back to Vraja and be loyal to their husbands. They refused to return as their minds were fixed upon him and longed for मोक्ष, and insisted they were his दासिस् and should be accepted. After some time he disappeared for their peace and redemption. They indulged in गीतम्, when the Lord appeared in their midst and shone like पुरुष among शक्तिस्। After consoling them he engaged them in a रासक्रीड, and finding them wearied, he engaged them in watersports and sports in the उपवन on the river-bank. There was no carnal act of sin. The Lord who had no बन्ध, did all this in sport.
१८: भा. X. Chaps. २७-33; Vi. IV. १२. १२.
Released Nanda from a reptile who turned out to be विद्याधर Sudars4ana. One day शन्खचूद a follower of कंसा seized some ladies of कृष्ण's party and ran away. They cried for succour. कृष्ण and राम followed. He left the women behind and ran. राम took charge of the ladies while कृष्ण pursued him, cut off his head and took the चूडामणि which he presented to राम. Killed अरीष्ट in the form of a bull who entered the Vraja and terrified the inmates.
१९: भा. X. Chaps. ३४-36; Vi. V. Chap. १४.
[page१-440+ ३७] Killed केशिन् who came to the Vraja in the guise of a horse and became केशव; killed one Vyoma in the guise of a गोपाल; seen milking cows with राम by अक्रूर who came to द्वारका at the instance of कंसा; agreed readily to start for मथुरा at अक्रूर's message. With अक्रूर, the two brothers arrived at मथुरा. and asked their friend to go home. He requested them to visit his house to which they agreed only after vanquishing कंसा. Next day afternoon, the two brothers and their Gopa followers went round the city and the women from terraces enjoyed the sight of कृष्ण and राम. On the way he met a washerman and asked for good clothes. On his refusal, he was killed, and all his clothes taken and distributed to his Gopas. Then they met a garland-maker सुदाम who voluntarily offered flower- garlands. Him he blessed and went. Next he saw a hunch- back woman carrying unguents to कंसा. For the mere asking she offered the whole of it to them. So कृष्ण con- verted her to a handsome lady who invited him to her house. This was agreed after finishing his work. Then they went through the bazaar and were rewarded with betels, sandal, etc., by merchants. Lastly they entered the place where the bow festival was held. कृष्ण broke it easily. The guards who attacked them were put to death. It was evening when they returned to the camp outside the city.
२०: भा. X. Chaps. ३७. ४२; Vi. V. १६. 7-१६, २३; Chaps. १८, १९.
On his way to the wrestlers' arena, कृष्ण vanquished कुवलयापीड with some effort. Taking its tusks, entered the enclosure with बलराम. Accepted challenge from the wrestler चानूर. The latter fell dead after fighting. The same fate met शल and तोशलक. Finding कंसा ready to attack his relations, कृष्ण overpowered him and killed him in a minute: condoled with the women of the dead and set his parents free; consoled his parents for their troubles and was embraced by them in love. Enthroned Ugrasena, as Yadus could not sit on the throne owing to a curse of ययाति. A regin of peace ushered in मथुरा.
२१: भा. X. Chaps. ४३-44 and ४
; Vi.

-३३; Chap. २०.
[page१-441+ ३८] Nanda and Gopas were sent back to Vraja with honours. उपनयनम् of कृष्ण. With बलराम Kr2s2n2a went to सान्दीपनि and learnt all arts in ६४ days. Hearing that सान्दीपनि's son was washed away by the sea at प्रभासा, कृष्ण went to the spot and was told by the seagod that an Asura पञ्चजन carried him off. Then he went to Yama's abode, and recovering his son, handed him over to the गुरु as गुरुदक्षिण and came home. Requested Uddhava to go to Vraja with a message from him to Nanda and Gopis that he would be visiting them shortly. As promised he went to Sairandhri's house with Uddhava. It was decorated according to rules of कामशास्त्र, and after a brief stay, left it for अक्रूर's with Uddhava and राम. अक्रूर extended a royal welcome. कृष्ण praised him as their गुरु and requested him to go to हास्तिनपुर् and find out the position of the पाण्डवस्. Returned to their residence.
२२: भा. X. ४५. २०-49; Chaps. ४६-48; Vi. V. २५. १९-31.
कृष्ण heard of the siege of मथुरा by जरासन्ध and was devis- ing a plan of attack when two chariots descended from heaven fully armoured. Also सुदर्शन, his चक्र and other weapons came down to him and to राम. राम took a chariot and the हल (plough), but was considered by जरा- sandha as a boy and not his equal. कृष्ण made defence arrangements at the four gates, and went out in his chariot of Garuda ensign by the northern gate to where Caidya and मागध were. Caidya's challenge and death; prevented राम from fettering जरासन्ध, and entered the city in victory and gave the spoils of war to Ugrasena, their king. Second and third defence of मथुरा. Prevented Kum- भाण्ड and कूपकर्ण from using माया in war by the application of विज्ञानास्त्र। Honoured after victory by the सभा of the Yadus.
२३: भा. X. Chaps. ५०-52 (v).
He next desired to see Gomanta and the hill fortress. Left with राम towards the south crossing the यमुना, and many towns and villages. Saw on the way परशुराम engaged in austere तपस् and bowed to him. परशुराम [page१-442+ ३९] suggested killing श्र्गालवासुदेव, a wicked chieftain of करवीरपुर at the foot of the Gomanta. When they reached the place, शृगालवासुदेव offered fight, and his head was cut off by कृष्ण. Welcomed by the citizens of करवीरपुर, they spent there four months after sending the spoils of war to मथुरा. Got up the hill Gomanta where गरुड met कृष्ण and placing his crown on his head, left. Reached मथुरा with a large army. Finding Yavana besieging the city and जरासन्ध leading the eighteenth expedition,, कृष्ण in consultation with राम resolved to build a fortress of १२ yojanas in the sea to place their kith and kin in security. So a city was built according to वास्तु शास्त्र to which Indra sent सुधर्मा and पारिजात। वरुण supplied horses and Kubera the eight निधिस्। It became a यादव settlement. Attacked by (काल) Yavana, कृष्ण unarmed fled to the cave where Mucukunda was asleep. Here Yavana was burnt to ashes by Mucukunda's energy. Mucukunda's surprise to see कृष्ण and his prayer for salva- tion. कृष्ण spoke of his future birth as ब्राह्मण and final salvation.
२४: Ib. X. Chap. ५३ (v) and ५०-51; Vi. V. Chaps. २२-3.
कृष्ण returned to Ugrasena at मथुरा, raised the siege of Yavana troops and went to द्वारका with his plunder. On the way जरासन्ध's army in मकर व्यूह attacked him but was broken by throwing a huge tree. Returned to द्वारका with spoils of war left by Yavanas. जरासन्ध's attack again when राम and कृष्ण fled to the Gomanta whose topcrest was burnt, while जरासन्ध thought they were dead they reached द्वारका safe.
२५: भा. X. Chap. ५२; Vi. V. २

.
Sent कृतवर्ण to ascertain from हास्तिनापुर whether पाण्डवस् had defeated Drupada. Married रुक्मिणि by the राक्षस form of mar- riage, defeating जरासन्ध and others of the Caidya party in battle. Received with due honours the ब्राह्मण mes- senger from रुक्मिणि and promised to do the needful. With the ब्राह्मण and राम, कृष्ण drove from आनर्तस् to Vidarbhas in a night. Was honoured by भीष्मक and allotted separate residence outside his capital. Ladies of [page१-443+ ३८] कुण्डिन said that कृष्ण was suitable to रुक्मिणि. Seeing रुक्मिणि returning from the Devi temple, he took her in his chariot in the midst of other kings and drove fast. जरा- sandha and others pursued but soon returned with dis- appointment. Rukmi's resolve to kill कृष्ण and then enter कुण्डिन. When he offered battle and was about to be killed, Rukmini appealed to the Lord to save her brother. At this he was tied to the chariot with his hair and moustache shaved. Advised by राम that punishment of रुक्मी was not in order. Married रुक्मिणि according to शाश्त्रस् amidst festivities in द्वारका. Owing to शिव's grace, got sacred sons of whom one was Pradyumna by Ruk- मिणी, being काम in a previous birth. Killed Sambara who stole the baby. Saw the lost Pradyumna and his wife रती in his residence, and hearing their account from नारद, embraced the couple. Present at Pradyumna's marriage.
२६: भा. X. Chaps. ५३-55; Vi. V. २
; Chap. २७; २

.
Requested सत्राजित to give the Syamantaka gem for their king but he refused. Suspected by सत्राजित to be res- ponsible for his brother Prasena's disappearance in the forest; recovered the jewel from जाम्बवन् after fight- ing for २८ days, and got also his daughter जाम्बवती in marriage. The jewel was returned to सत्राजित in the public assembly. Married सत्राजित's daughter सत्यभामा, and when the jewel was offered, it was returned. Went with राम to the Kurus after the rumoured death of the पाण्ड- vas and Kunti; met the पाण्डवस् at पाञ्चाल city in the guise of ब्राह्मणस्; killed शतधन्वन्, the murderer of his father-in-law सत्राजित. Sent for अक्रूर and asked him to exhibit Syamantaka in his possession, and returned it to him afterwards.
२७: भा. X. Chaps. ५६-57; Br.
III. 7

. ३०१; ३६. १५ and २१; ६८-28; ७१. ४६-96; M. ४५. ३४; Vi. IV. १३. ६४-98. १४२-157.
कृष्ण once went to हास्तिनापुर to see the पाण्डवस् and was heartily welcomed. Paid respects to युधिष्ठिर and भीम, embraced Arjuna and received respects from Nakula and Sahadeva. कुन्ती welcomed him also. When he was spending that winter there, he went to the forest [page१-444+ ४१] with Arjuna for hunting and there met an accomplished lady when Arjuna addressed. Hearing that she was the daughter of the Sun waiting to marry कृष्ण, the latter took her home. In the meantime कृष्ण asked विश्वकर्मा to build a city for the पाण्डवस्. Acting as Arjuna's charioteer, he caused the खाण्डव forest to be given over to fire. Returned to द्वारका and married कालिन्दी, Sun's daughter. Then he married मित्रविन्दा of Avanti, an aunt's daughter. Received सत्या, daughter of Nagnajit of अयोध्या by curb- ing the ferocity of seven bulls, with a large dowry of chariots, elephants and treasure. Jealous kings were driven away by Arjuna. Married another aunt's daughter भद्रा. Took लक्ष्मणा, daughter of the Madra king and thousands of maidens from Naraka's harem.
२८: भा. X. Chap. ५८.
Indra came one day to द्वारका and reported to कृष्ण the mischief done to him by Naraka. Entering प्राग्ज्योतिष, कृष्ण pulled down ramparts and walls and cut off Mura's five heads. His seven sons attacked him led by पाठ in vain. Naraka also attacked and had his head cut off. कृष्ण entered the city welcomed by its people, saw मणिपर्वत of Indra and the umbrella of वरुण and gave them back to them. Earth, mother of Naraka came before कृष्ण and handed over the कुण्डलस् of Aditi, informing him that Naraka was her son by the touch of Hari in वाराह form. Then he entered the harem of the Asura and sent away
(some

sons. With सत्यभामा he visited Indra's abode and after giving the कुण्डलस् to Aditi, he came back with पारिजात against Indra's will, because his queen wanted it. He enjoyed the company of all his wives, taking a separate form for each wife. Indra's attack on कृष्ण with gods like वरुण, वायु, etc., for taking away पारिजात। Their defeat and Indra's apology. कृष्ण consoled him. Welcomed back in द्वारका.
३०: भा. X. ५९. २२-45; Chap. ६५ (v) to ६७ (v); Vi. V. Chap. ३०; ३

.
[page१-445+ ३७] Love quarrel with his consort रुक्मिणी described. Once when कृष्ण was sitting at leisure, रुक्मिणि who was nearby fanned him. कृष्ण indulged in fun and asked her how she chose a poor fellow like him leaving princes of equal status with her, and added that he was willing to let her go and marry a powerful क्षत्रिय prince. This put out poor Ruk- मिणि who wept bitterly, speaking words showing her unflinching loyalty to him. Noticing her sincerity कृष्ण consoled her that he simply cut a joke. He said that she knew him to be Hari to whom राजऋषिस् like अङ्ग, नहुष and Gaya had dedicated their lives leaving their kingdoms, and that ब्रह्मा and शिव sang his praises. कृष्ण assured her of his loyalty to her. In this way he led a household life just like an ordinary mortal. Each one of his eight chief queens gave birth to ten sons, and each thought that कृष्ण was only living with her, as there was a कृष्ण by the side of each lady including the

of Naraka's harem. He played with them blindman's buff, exchanging betels, scents, etc. The chief queens were Rukmini, सत्यभामा, जाम्ब- वती, सत्या, कालिन्दी, माद्रि, मित्रविन्दा, and भद्रा. Attended Aniruddha's marriage with रोचना at भोजकट. Heard from नारद of Aniruddha's imprisonment by बाण of

arms and besieged शोनितपुर. Defeated शिव who came on बाणा's behalf and at शिव's request, let बाण go with his four arms remaining. Returned to द्वारका with Aniruddha and उषा.
३१: भा. X. Chaps. ६०-63; Vi. IV. १५. ३०-4; V. ३३. १२-53.
Heard from a ब्राह्मण of the externment of पाण्ड- vas to the forest, and riding on a chariot with सत्यभामा, met them and consoled them; came back with सुभद्रा and Abhimanyu. Heard a report of a huge lizard in a well, and lifting it up, he found it to be a divinity who revealed him- self as king नृग and who went to heaven. Taught the citizens of द्वारक on the invisilability of ब्राह्मणस्’ property.
३२: भा. X. Chap. ६४.
[page१-446+ ३७] कृष्ण heard of पौण्ड्रक's invasion of द्वारका in his absence. Had a message from him either to give up the title of वासुदेव or offer battle. Ugrasena and others laughed at this. कृष्ण went to काशी and had the heads of पौण्ड्रक and his ally cut off and their army destroyed. कृष्ण's return to द्वारक. An आभिचार Agni was sent by पौण्ड्- raka's son through the grace of शिव but was vanquished by Hari's चक्र। By his योग power कृष्ण appeared at the mansions of each of his

wives, engaged in a normal domestic life. When नारद entered every house, he saw the same कृष्ण in each; got up early in the morning and meditated on Brahman; gave cows, etc., to the ब्राह्मणस्, saw first ghee, then mirror, cows, gods, etc. Heard from a messenger of the difficulties of kings imprisoned by जरा- sandha. Advised by Uddhava to vanquish जरासन्ध with the aid of भीम at युधिष्ठिर's राजसूय। कृष्ण's route to हास्तिनापुर where he was received by the पाण्डवस्. द्रौपदी welcomed his wives and, these were put up com- fortably. Hearing जरासन्ध still unconquered, कृष्ण with भीम and Arjuna went to Girivraja in ब्राह्मणस्’ disguise and asked for meals. They then threw off their disguise and called him to battle in which भीम won. After releasing prisoners, कृष्ण enthroned Sahadeva, son of जरासन्ध.
३३: Ib. X. Chaps. ६७-73; M. ४७, १४; Vi. V. ३

.
The kings thus released after the fall of जरासन्ध were

, praised the Lord and requested that they might ever remember Him. कृष्ण asked them to go back to their places and assume charge of governments by ruling righteously. Sahadeva arranged their bath, dress and meals, after which they left for where युधिष्ठिर and his family were. Received the first honour in the राजसूय of युधिष्ठिर when शिशुपाल protested in a vilifying speech. His head was cut off. Lived in हास्तिनापुर for some months at the request of युधिष्ठीर and others. Attended to अर्घ्य and पाद्य for ब्राह्मणस् in the राजसूय। Welcomed नारद who informed him of the necessity of vanquishing शाल्व. Left for द्वारका hearing of its blockade by शाल्व [page१-447+ ३७] who applied illusory powers. कृष्ण broke his car and killed him. कृष्ण went as an ambassador of the पाण्डवस् to Dur- yodhana. He was sought to be made prisoner in vain; came back determined to declare war. In the war served as Arjuna's charioteer, and after the war कृष्ण condoled with धृतराष्ट्र and after anointing युधिष्ठीर, returned to द्वारका. One day there came Kucaila, a ब्राह्मण classmate of कृष्ण, a poor man with many children. Induced by his wife he visited कृष्ण who welcomed him with रुक्मिणि, indulged in talks of old school days, partook of the पृथुक rice which Kucaila's wife had sent, and sent him away after keeping him for a night.

Left for स्यमन्तपञ्चक for solar eclipse, met Gopis there and taught them the nature of the Absolute. Sages waited on him and praised his glory. His joy at Vasudeva's sacrifice. Honoured Nanda. Praised by his father, कृष्ण replied that आत्म is only one. At the request of देवकी to get back all her sons killed by कम्सा, कृष्ण entered Sutalam and with leave of Bali, took them to his mother who embraced them in affection. These children who were degraded gods gained their old form and went to heaven.
३५: Ib. X. Chaps. ८२-85.
सुभद्रा was his sister, and Arjuna carried her off with his knowledge and against the wish of बलराम. He went with sages to मिथिला where was his ब्राह्मण devotee श्रु- tadeva. The latter and the king मैथिला welcomed him and requested him to stay. कृष्ण did not like to disoblige them and so stayed in both houses taking two different forms, thus purifying Nimi line, and pleasing श्रुतदेव.
३६: Ib. X. Chap. ८६.
Performed अश्वमेध sacrifice in the course of which he had to go to वैकुण्ठ with Arjuna to recover the lost children of a द्वारका Bra1hman2a who preferred a complaint. After return with the lost boy, he had his अवभृत cele- [page१-448+ ३८] brated in the यमुना. Then he continued his righteous rule and spent a good time in द्वारका enjoying pleasures with his chosen wives.
३७: Ib. X. Chaps. ८८-90.
His service to the world was to kill Daityas and relieve the burden of the Earth. Resolved to destroy the Yadu race and reach his eternal abode; approved of the curse of the sages against the Yadu race. ब्रह्मा and other gods visited him, appealing to him to go back to वैकुण्ठ. He agreed. Uddhava expressed a wish to follow him but was advised by कृष्ण to lead a righteous life. Incidentally कृष्ण narrated to him the conversation of a certain अवधूत and Yadu. Insisting on यम and नियम, and duties incumbent on वर्ण and आश्रम। Then he described who was said to be in bondage, who was a free man and a righteous person, and he also explained the need and importance of सत्सन्ग। He proceeded to instruct Uddhava on the nature of the गुणस्, and their causes, laying emphasis on सत्व गुण। Then he explained भक्ति, ध्यान, सिद्धिस् and their nature. He afterwards narrated the विभूतिस् of Hari, described the dharmas of वर्ण and आश्रम, explained what was ज्ञान and विज्ञान, giving a list of duties to be observed by all. He further instructed on the three योगस्--ज्ञान, कर्म and भक्ति, on the Vedas, and on the principles of साङ्ख्य and साङ्ख्यविधि। He then narrated the story of an Avanti ब्राह्मण who turned out ascetic after being a miser. He enumerated the different characteristics of the three गुणस् and the evil effects of bad association, recapitulating क्रिया- योग, ज्ञान योग अन्द् भक्ति योग। Lastly Uddhava was advised to go to Badari.

Advised his relations to go to प्रभास, and there deluded by him, they fought among themselves and died. बलराम also met his death. कृष्ण heard this while sit- ting under a पिप्पल tree. A hunter जरा by name aimed his shaft at his foot little thinking that it was the Lord. Coming to know that it was कृष्ण he regretted much. कृष्ण consoled him and permitted him to go to Heaven. [page१-449+ ४४] कृष्ण addressed his charioteer दामक to go to द्वारका, and advise the people there to leave for Hastinapura with Arjuna. Invited by gods कृष्ण entered his धाम, while his wives entered fire.
